answer: Sequential latency ledger. Each identity must complete a fixed series of live, randomly scheduled challenge rounds; the system records timing fingerprints as a prism separating genuine agents from scripted bursts. Missed rounds forfeit progress, so an attacker running N parallel identities pays N times the real-time waiting cost plus coordination overhead at each wharf checkpoint. Only identities surviving the full lagoon sequence can transact, making mass registration expensive in wall-clock hours rather than money.
